newsitem.title: DENMARK: INTERVIEW-Irish cargo cheers Singapore Airlines.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Irish cargo cheers Singapore Airlines.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd said Dublin was the solution for filling its freighters and that it would rejig its timetable to take advantage of high-value, high-tech Irish goods.

Jens Heide, cargo manager Scandinavia and Finland for Singapore Airlines, told Reuters that starting in its summer timetable it would operate two of its Boeing 747 freighter twice weekly through Dublin and Copenhagen.

Currently only one of the freighters operates from Singapore, through Dublin and on to Copenhagen and back to Singapore, making technical stops in Dehli and Dubai. The other flies to Moscow on its way to Copenhagen and stops in Delhi.
In October 1996 the airline started a weekly service between Singapore and Dublin with Irish hi-tech exports allocated 12 to 15 tonnes of cargo capacity.
"We are selling half the cargo inbound to Dublin. Yields are quite high," Heide said in an interview. "We want to operate three times weekly to Dublin within the next year."
He said goods to Dublin, which could fill inbound freighters, was the perfect match for Copenhagen, which was heavy on the export side but weak on inbound.
"We are strong in the export side so it matches well with Copenhagen," Heide said.

Heide said the carrier was aiming to sell long-haul as much as possible and that the majority of its cargo from the Nordic region went to the Southwest Pacific region, including about half to New Zealand and Australia.
"We are trying to sell long-haul as much as possible. The highest yields we can get are from Australia and New Zealand," he said. From Finland even more went to that part of the world.
"Some 90 percent of our volumes from Finland is to Australia and New Zealand," Heide said.

Heide said the Danish market was the most competitive among the other Nordic markets. "Denmark consists of a lot of medium sized shippers. Finland is like Sweden, there are a few big industries," he said.

Singapore Airlines said last week it had taken a local decision to raise freight rates from Denmark and Norway by five to seven percent in its summer timetable but that it would keep rates from Finland and Sweden the same.
"The currencies have strengthened since we adjusted the rates last time," Heide said.
"Here in Scandinavia we tend to keep the same rate level. The last adjustment will make this gap closer again," he said.
The airline wanted to avoid a situation where cargo space was cheaper from Denmark than just across the border in Sweden.
Copenhagen Airport is Singapore Airline's cargo hub in the Nordic region and it trucks goods from Sweden, Finland and Norway to the region.
From Norway the main export was salmon, from Sweden it was Ericsson telecommunications and from Denmark it was a mixed bag of water pumps, electronic measuring instruments and chemicals.
At the moment it was negotiating deals only through forwarders and made some three-party deals which included shippers, the airline and the forwarder.
Heide said there was probably too much capacity from Stockholm but said this would not prevent the airline from possibly adding more capacity to the region.
"At the moment there is too much capacity. I'm not against capacity. I think the skies should be open to whatever cargo capacity wanted to operate to Stockholm," he said.
